protocol.description:
This protocol aims at describing outputs in a way which is more in line with the concept of an output on desktop oriented systems.
Some information are more specific to the concept of an output for a desktop oriented system and may not make sense in other applications. It is not meant to replace the core wl_output events.
This protocol is meant to be used together with the core wl_output protocol.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is experimental and backward incompatible changes may be made. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes are done by bumping the version number in the protocol and interface names and resetting the interface version. Once the protocol is to be declared stable, the 'z' prefix and the version number in the protocol and interface names will be removed.

interface.name: zxdg_output_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory interface for xdg_output objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Using this request a client can tell the server that it is not going to use the xdg_output_manager object anymore.
Any objects already created through this instance are not affected.

request.name: get_xdg_output

description.summary: create an xdg output from a wl_output

request.description: This creates a new xdg_output object for the given wl_output.

interface.name: zxdg_output_v1
interface.description:
An xdg_output describes part of the compositor geometry.
This typically corresponds to a monitor that displays part of the compositor space.
For objects version 3 onwards, after all xdg_output properties have been sent (when the object is created and when properties have changed), a wl_output.done event is sent. This allows changes to the xdg_output properties to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Using this request a client can tell the server that it is not going to use the xdg_output object anymore.

event.name: logical_position

description.summary: position of the output within the global compositor space

event.description: The position event describes the location of the wl_output within the global compositor space.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x position within the global compositor space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y position within the global compositor space

event.name: logical_size

description.summary: size of the output in the global compositor space

event.description: The logical_size event describes the size of the output in the global compositor space.

event.name: done

description.summary: all information about the output have been sent

event.description:
This event is sent after all other properties of an xdg_output have been sent.
This allows changes to the xdg_output properties to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events.
For objects version 3 onwards, this event is deprecated. Compositors are not required to send it anymore and must send wl_output.done instead.

event.name: name
event.description:
Many compositors will assign user-friendly names to their outputs, show them to the user, allow the user to refer to an output, etc. The client may wish to know this name as well to offer the user similar behaviors.
The name is a UTF-8 string with no convention defined for its contents. Each name is unique among all wl_output globals. The name is only guaranteed to be unique for the compositor instance.
The same output name is used for all clients (e.g. a console background, lockscreen, panel, ...).
Names are guaranteed to not change on a given compositor instance.

event.name: description
event.description:
Many compositors can produce human-readable descriptions for their outputs. The client may wish to know this description as well, e.g. for output selection purposes.
The description is a UTF-8 string with no convention defined for its contents. The description is not guaranteed to be unique among all wl_output globals. Examples might be 'Foocorp 11" Class 3' for a LVDS panel or 'Virtual Output' for a virtual sink.
Descriptions are guaranteed to not change on a given compositor instance.
